answer: Every agent identity escrows a bond on itself alone, never pooled, before it can emit rewards. A second account needs fresh capital and full mining cost from zero. Funding lineage is traced, so a linked parent and child are slashed together, and behaviour clustering groups accounts with matching timing even if the routine is polished like a sonnet. The farmer risks a whole stake per fake identity for a marginal emission share: N identities cost N stakes plus N histories. Like copper, weight must be mined before it is spent; no tint, not even saffron, hides a linked cluster.
